intro: Honghub Sakon Hotel, also known simply as Honghub Sakon, is a clean, no-frills small hotel in Sakon Nakhon town · The selling point reviewers agree on is that the rooms are new, clean and quiet, with a handy location walking distance to Sakon Nakhon Bus Terminal 2 and near Robinson · The hotel has just 17 rooms built around a Clean / Comfort / Convenient concept — no pool, no breakfast, but you get free parking, free Wi-Fi and free bikes to borrow · Rooms start at about THB 659/night · Scored 8.0 from 9 reviews on Trip.com

body.html: Overview and who it suits — To put it as briefly as possible, Honghub Sakon Hotel is a small hotel that sells "peace of mind" more than luxury · It isn't a big hotel with a wide lobby or a swimming pool, and it isn't trying to be one either · What it sets out to do is offer rooms that are clean, new and quiet, in a location with easy access in and out of Sakon Nakhon town, especially for people travelling by bus since it's within walking distance of Sakon Nakhon Bus Terminal 2 · The concept the owner spells out is three clear words — Clean / Comfort / Convenient · From real reviews, the people it suits best are drivers who want safe free parking, travellers here on short business, people who get off the bus and want a bed nearby, and couples or small families on a modest budget who still want a clean, quiet room · For anyone after a hotel with lots of amenities, breakfast, a pool, or the full service of a big hotel, this may not be the answer, because at its core it's a small property focused on "sleeping well in a clean room" — not a destination for spending the whole day inside the hotel

Location and getting around — What makes Honghub Sakon Hotel interesting is its position in Sakon Nakhon town, on the Tha Choeng Chum subdistrict side · The clearest highlight is that it's a short walk from Sakon Nakhon Bus Terminal 2, a big advantage for anyone arriving by bus — get off, wheel your bag over and check in without needing another ride · It's also near Robinson Sakon Nakhon, the city's main mall with restaurants, a cinema and a supermarket · Around the hotel there are convenience stores, local eateries and food within walking distance · On the sightseeing side it's close to Wat Phra That Narai Cheng Weng, a few minutes' drive away, and Sakon Nakhon Rajabhat University, about 2 km away · For those flying in, Sakon Nakhon Airport (SNO) is around 6 km away, roughly a 9–10 min drive — very close compared with many hotels in town · Nong Han, Isan's large freshwater lake, is about 5 km away · One thing to note is that this location isn't in the "old town" right by Phra That Choeng Chum or the morning market like some hotels; if you mainly plan to explore the old town on foot you may need a short ride, but if you're coming by car or focused on bus and mall convenience, this location works very well

"Got off the bus at Bus Terminal 2 and walked straight here, no extra ride needed. The room was new and clean, nice and quiet, slept well, and there's free parking too. Really great for anyone here on business."

Room types and decor — Honghub Sakon Hotel is a small hotel with around 17 rooms in total · Going by the booking platforms and the hotel's own website, the main room types are Twin Hub (two single beds), Deluxe Double or Deluxe Hub (one queen bed), Deluxe Twin, and Family Triple / Family Hub, which pairs a single bed with a queen for a small family or three people · The decor is simple, in a bright, clean tone, nothing flashy, leaning more practical than showy · Every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV (cable), a fridge, a private bathroom, a hairdryer and free toiletries · The point reviews agree on most is the cleanliness and newness of the rooms — many say the rooms look new, neatly kept, the AC cools well, and most importantly it's quiet and easy to sleep in · Some reviews praise the rooms as bigger than expected for the price · There's daily housekeeping, which keeps the rooms feeling fresh throughout the stay · These are rooms with "nothing fancy, but complete and clean in a way that lets you sleep well" — which matches the hotel's concept exactly

Facilities — Let's be upfront first: Honghub Sakon Hotel is a small hotel with no swimming pool, no fitness room and no spa, so anyone hoping to take a dip or work out at the hotel won't find it here · But what it does offer, and what reviews rate well, are the basics you actually use every day · There's free private parking, a big deal for self-drivers — many reviews mention the peace of mind of safe parking · There's free Wi-Fi in both the rooms and common areas, free bikes to borrow for riding around the area, a shared lounge with a TV to sit and relax, a small garden, laundry service (surcharge), a front desk with a wake-up service, and convenience stores/vending machines nearby · There are also extras like a shuttle and airport transfer (surcharge), a taxi-call service, and help booking tours/tickets for those who didn't drive · Overall the facilities here fall into the "right-sized for the price" category — not a lot, but complete in what travellers really use

About the pool — Let's make this clear because it's a common search: Honghub Sakon Hotel has no swimming pool · As a small hotel of just 17 rooms on a limited footprint, a pool isn't something a property like this would have · If a pool is genuinely something you need on this trip, consider a larger hotel in Sakon Nakhon that has one, such as the 3–4 star hotels in the city centre · But if you're looking for a clean, quiet place to rest or to base a business trip, the lack of a pool won't ruin the experience, because the appeal here is cleanliness, quiet and location — not resort-style amenities

Food and eats around the hotel — Another thing to know before booking is that Honghub Sakon Hotel does not serve breakfast and has no in-house restaurant · That's normal for a small self-catering property · But the good news is the location helps a lot, with convenience stores, made-to-order eateries and local food within walking distance or a short bike ride · Importantly it's near Robinson Sakon Nakhon, which has a food court, cafes and a full supermarket, so meals are no problem · Many past guests say to use this to your advantage — head out for proper Isan food around town, or grab snacks from a convenience store to enjoy in the room · Rooms have a fridge for chilling food and drinks, which makes it easy for anyone who likes to stock up · In short, food relies mainly on places outside, but the location makes it easy to find and never in short supply

Service — Service is another point that earns praise in real reviews · Even as a small hotel, most voices say the staff are friendly, look after guests well and can help with various things — check-in, restaurant tips, calling a ride, and sorting out parking · Being a small hotel actually works in its favour here, with care that's fairly personal and uncomplicated · There's a front desk and a wake-up service, handy for anyone who has to be up early to catch onward transport or run errands · Extras like airport transfers and help booking tickets/tours are available for those who didn't drive (surcharges per item) · To be straight with you, since this is a small property that may not have staff on duty 24 hours like a big hotel, getting in touch ahead about check-in/check-out times or extra services helps keep everything smooth

What real reviews say (both praise and gripes) — Pulling together Trip.com and other booking platforms, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: rooms are new and clean, the atmosphere is quiet and easy to sleep in, the AC cools well, the location is handy within walking distance of Bus Terminal 2 and near Robinson, parking is free and safe, staff service is good and friendly, and there's daily housekeeping · Many sum it up as "good value for a small hotel in Sakon Nakhon town" · On the gripes side: the things mentioned are a drain smell in the bathroom of some rooms that a few reviews ran into, the fact that the hotel has no breakfast and no restaurant so you have to eat out, the limited facilities that come with being a small hotel (no pool, no fitness room), and a location that, while convenient for buses and the mall, isn't right by the old town or Phra That Choeng Chum · Most of these gripes are about setting expectations to match a "budget small hotel" rather than being major problems

"Clean, new room, quiet, lovely staff, and parking I felt at ease about. The only downsides were a slight drain smell in the bathroom and no breakfast, but you can walk out to eat. At this price it's really very okay."

Price comparison and value — The starting price at Honghub Sakon Hotel is about THB 659/night and the average runs around THB 783/night per the booking platforms, moving up and down with room type and timing · Compared with other hotels in Sakon Nakhon town, that price sits in the mid-range, leaning budget — a bit above the cheapest older hotels, but in exchange you get rooms that are newer and cleaner · What makes it good value are the things you don't pay extra for, like free parking, free Wi-Fi and free bikes, plus a location that saves on transport if you arrive by bus · The thing to subtract in your head is that breakfast isn't included, so you'll need to add the cost of breakfast out · For anyone who values cleanliness, quiet and a walk-to-the-bus-terminal location over big-hotel amenities, a price at this level is reasonable and good value in its own way

What to know before booking — A few things help make the stay smoother · One, since it's a small hotel with just 17 rooms, rooms fill fast during festivals and long weekends, especially around Sakon Nakhon's big merit-making events like the Wax Castle Procession and the end of Buddhist Lent (October) — book ahead · Two, if you're arriving by bus, make the most of the walking distance from Bus Terminal 2, and let them know your arrival time ahead for an easy check-in · Three, the hotel has no breakfast, so plan breakfast ahead or use the proximity to Robinson and convenience stores to your advantage · Four, a few reviews ran into a drain smell in the bathroom; if you're worried, take a look at the room at check-in and tell the staff right away · Five, check-in starts around 1:00 PM and check-out is before 12:00 PM; if you arrive early, contact the hotel about luggage storage · Six, choose free cancellation up front if your plans aren't firm, since small properties adjust prices by season

Bottom line — From all the real reviews, Honghub Sakon Hotel is the small hotel that suits anyone who wants a clean, new and quiet bed in a location with easy access in and out of Sakon Nakhon town, especially people arriving by bus or driving themselves · The walk to Bus Terminal 2, the proximity to Robinson, free parking, and clean, quiet rooms make it good value among the city's budget small hotels · If you're after a swimming pool, included breakfast, or big-hotel amenities, this isn't the answer, and you should look at the 3–4 star hotels in the city centre instead · But for a trip where you want a simple place that does the job of "sleeping well in a clean room" at an affordable price, Honghub Sakon Hotel is an honest match for its Clean / Comfort / Convenient concept

faq.a: Honghub Sakon Hotel (Honghub Sakon) is at 272/37 Tha Choeng Chum subdistrict, Mueang Sakon Nakhon district in Sakon Nakhon town · The standout is that it's walking distance to Sakon Nakhon Bus Terminal 2 and near Robinson · It's close to Wat Phra That Narai Cheng Weng and Sakon Nakhon Rajabhat University (~2 km) · Sakon Nakhon Airport is about 6 km away, roughly a 9–10 min drive

faq.q: What's the starting price at Honghub Sakon Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 659/night and average around THB 783/night per the booking platforms · Room types include Twin Hub (two singles), Deluxe Double/Deluxe Hub (queen), Deluxe Twin, and Family Triple/Family Hub for a small family · It's a small hotel with around 17 rooms, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Does Honghub Sakon Hotel have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: It has neither a swimming pool nor breakfast · It's a small self-catering hotel focused on clean rooms and a handy location · But it's near Robinson, convenience stores and local restaurants, so food is easy to find, and rooms have a fridge to chill things · There's free parking, free Wi-Fi, and free bikes to borrow

faq.q: Who is Honghub Sakon Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for people arriving by bus, driving themselves, or here on business who want a clean, new and quiet room at an affordable price · It's walking distance to Bus Terminal 2 and near Robinson · If you want a swimming pool, included breakfast, or to stay right by the old town / Phra That Choeng Chum, Sakon Nakhon town has other options that suit better

faq.q: What are the check-in and check-out times at Honghub Sakon Hotel?
faq.a: Check-in starts at 1:00 PM (until about 10:00 PM) and check-out is before 12:00 PM · If you arrive early or come on a late-night bus, it's best to contact the hotel ahead about your arrival time and luggage storage, since it's a small property that may not have staff on duty 24 hours
